new_statements.quote: Stress or prominence occurs on the final syllable of the stem. It does not shift when a suffix or clitic is added to the stem. [...] Stress is predominantly indicated through increased intensity occasionally accompanied by a slightly lengthened vowel. In monomorphemic words, stress occurs on the final syllable [...] In multimorphemic words, the stressed syllable is always the final syllable of the stem, even when an affix or clitic is added. [...] The actual placement of the stem in the surface grammatical word and the number of affixes is irrelevant. Stress placement is only dependent on the stem. All syllable types can occur in stressed and unstressed syllables. There is no indication of vowel reduction or tone loss on unstressed syllables.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress is fixed on the last syllable of the stem: word-final in monomorphemic words and in prefixed words, but enclitics/suffixes (negative -hi, possessive -na, -ʔɛ, -ɲa, modal -ra) are extrametrical and stress stays on the stem-final syllable; in compounds stress is on the final syllable of the whole compound stem. Stress is weight-insensitive, cued by intensity (and slight lengthening), independent of the tone system; nasal vowels are (with listed exceptions) restricted to the stressed syllable.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Fn. 102 (p. 162): 'Secondary stress can also be found in some words, but further investigation is beyond the scope of this paper.' No placement rule given.
new_statements.exceptions: None to stress placement itself; author notes (fn. 102) that because stress is 'constant and immovable' it might better be called a prominent syllable. Exceptions discussed concern nasal vowels occurring outside the stressed syllable (certain enclitics, first members of compounds). Fn. 103: one tone sandhi process (sec. 5.2.2) may involve floating-tone attraction to the stressed syllable.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the stem within the grammatical word (prefix + stem + enclitics); statements based on elicited words, frames, sentences and texts from six speakers of San Miguel Soyaltepec municipality (Temascal area), Oaxaca, recorded 2005-2009. Language is tonal (4 levels + contours); stress described as 'not a very active process' and unmarked in the rest of the work.
new_statements.identity_note: Beal's data are from six speakers in the San Miguel Soyaltepec municipality (Temascal / Miguel Alemán dam resettlement area), Oaxaca — Soyaltepec Mazatec proper, ISO vmp, glottocode soya1237; no sub-dialect distinction drawn.

sources.note: Sec. 3.6 'Stress' (pp. 162-163): stress/prominence falls on the final syllable of the stem; does not shift when suffixes or enclitics are added (prefixes irrelevant); cued mainly by intensity, sometimes slight vowel lengthening; no vowel reduction or tone loss in unstressed syllables; nasal vowels licensed only in stressed syllables; secondary stress exists in some words but not investigated; tone independent of stress (fn. 103 notes one possible floating-tone attraction to stressed syllable).
